writing.sample_en:
【参考范文 · 166 词】写作无唯一标准答案，以下为达标示范
Today increasing importance is being attached to cultivating college students' team spirit. Both universities and future employers have realized that few achievements today are the work of a single hand, so this quality truly deserves our attention.
There are convincing reasons behind this trend. First, almost every modern task, from a laboratory experiment to a business start-up, demands that people with different strengths pool their efforts; without cooperation, even talented individuals can accomplish little. Second, working in a team teaches students to communicate patiently, respect different opinions, and share responsibility, all of which are qualities that textbooks alone can never provide. A student who once relied only on personal effort, for instance, may finally learn to trust others after completing a group project together.
For these reasons, team spirit should never be treated as something optional. Colleges ought to design more group tasks, and students themselves should step out of their comfort zones and embrace cooperation, because it is teamwork that turns scattered abilities into real strength.

cloze.title: 2022年12月·第3套 英语六级完形填空（选词填空） · 26–35 题答案与解析

passages.en: American colleges and universities are using 64 percent less coal than they did a decade ago, burning 700,000 tons last year, down from 2 million tons in 2008, the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) said in a report __(26)__ yesterday.
passages.zh: 美国能源信息署（EIA）在昨日发布的一份报告中称，美国各高校目前使用的煤炭比十年前少了64%，去年燃烧了70万吨煤炭，而2008年为200万吨。

passages.en: All 57 schools that were burning coal in 2008 are using less now, and 20 have __(27)__ coal completely, EIA found.
passages.zh: EIA发现，2008年使用煤炭的57所学校如今都减少了煤炭用量，其中20所已经完全弃用煤炭。

passages.en: Most universities have turned to natural gas as a __(28)__ , with state funding backing the fuel switch.
passages.zh: 大多数大学都转而使用天然气作为替代能源，州政府的资金支持了这一燃料转换。

passages.en: While academic institutions use less than 0.1 percent of U.S. coal burned for power, campus coal use has a history dating back to the 1800s when __(29)__ to power was scarce.
passages.zh: 虽然各学术机构使用的煤炭占美国用于发电的煤炭总量不到0.1%，但校园煤炭使用的历史可以追溯到19世纪，当时电力供应十分匮乏。

passages.en: Many universities still operate their own power plants. The Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 encouraged more electricity generation by allowing institutions to sell __(30)__ power to utilities.
passages.zh: 许多大学仍在运营自己的发电厂。1978年的《公共事业监管政策法》允许各机构向公用事业公司出售剩余电力，从而鼓励了更多发电。

passages.en: But EIA noted many coal-fired universities have signed onto the American College and University Presidents Climate Commitment, which was launched in 2007.
passages.zh: 但EIA指出，许多使用燃煤发电的大学已经签署了《美国高校校长气候承诺》，该承诺于2007年启动。

passages.en: About 665 schools are part of the program, which aims to __(31)__ greenhouse gas emissions. Thirty percent of the participants have pledged to be carbon __(32)__ within 20 years.
passages.zh: 约有665所学校参加了这一计划，该计划旨在大幅削减温室气体排放。参与者中有30%承诺在20年内实现碳中和。

passages.en: The Sierra Club's Beyond Coal campaign, which also leads campaigns for universities to withdraw their __(33)__ in coal and other fossil fuels, lists 22 schools that have pledged to move "beyond coal," including Clemson University, Indiana University, Ohio University, Penn State University, the University of Louisville and the University of Tennessee, Knoxville.
passages.zh: 塞拉俱乐部的“超越煤炭”运动还发起了要求大学撤回对煤炭及其他化石燃料投资的活动，该运动列出了22所承诺“超越煤炭”的学校，其中包括克莱姆森大学、印第安纳大学、俄亥俄大学、宾夕法尼亚州立大学、路易斯维尔大学和田纳西大学诺克斯维尔分校。

passages.en: The largest coal use __(34)__ at colleges were in Michigan, Missouri, Tennessee and Indiana. Indiana's universities alone cut coal __(35)__ by 81 percent between 2008 and 2015.
passages.zh: 大学煤炭用量削减幅度最大的州是密歇根州、密苏里州、田纳西州和印第安纳州。仅印第安纳州的大学在2008年至2015年间就将煤炭消耗量削减了81%。

passages.en: During the same period, Michigan made an 80 percent cut and Tennessee cut back by 94 percent at state institutions.
passages.zh: 同期，密歇根州削减了80%，田纳西州的公立机构则削减了94%。

wordbank.gloss: 放弃，抛弃（动词过去式/过去分词）；被遗弃的（形容词）
（接近/使用的）机会、途径、入口（名词，常用 access to）；接入、访问（动词）

rows.text: K) released动词
「a report ___ yesterday」report 后修饰、yesterday 锁过去时 → 过去分词作后置定语
release a report = 发布报告，是固定搭配 said in a report __(26)__ yesterday 中 release a report（发布报告）是新闻语篇里的典型搭配，与「EIA 昨天发布的一份报告里说……」语义完全咬合。
G)mobilizedmobilize a report 不通 mobilize 与「人力、资源、军队」搭，从不修饰 report；语义上「动员一份报告」也讲不通。
A) abandoned动词
「have ___ coal completely」现在完成时缺过去分词

「彻底放弃燃煤」与全文「减煤」主线完全吻合 20 have __(27)__ coal completely 与 American colleges and universities are using 64 percent less coal than they did a decade ago 形成程度递进——大多数学校少用，20 所「彻底放弃」。abandon coal 是脱煤议题的高频表达。

G)mobilized「动员了煤炭」与「停用煤炭」方向相反 mobilize 意为「动员、调动」，have mobilized coal completely 等于「已经把煤完全动员起来用」，与「彻底放弃」截然相反，逻辑错位。 K)releasedrelease coal 不通且与上下文矛盾 release coal 不是常用搭配（release 多与 report、information、emissions 搭），且与「使用」无关；后续 26 题更需要 released 来搭配 report，此处不应抢用。

最具迷惑性的错误词是 K) —— released 词性形态都对，最易抢走 27 题。have ___ coal completely 处 K)released 形态完全合规，且 release 在新闻语体里高频；但 release coal 不是自然搭配，且 26 题 a report ___ yesterday 才是 released 的归属。考生若不按「先易后难、用过即划」的顺序，容易把 K 提前用到 27 题、导致 26 题再也找不到合适的过去分词。防坑：先做 26 题（因为 a report released yesterday 的搭配更硬），把 K 划走，27 题就自然落到 abandoned 上。
L) replacement名词
不定冠词 a 后的空 → 单数名词
「转向天然气作为替代品」语义最贴 Most universities have turned to natural gas as a __(28)__, with state funding backing the fuel switch. 句末 the fuel switch（这次燃料切换）直接点题——天然气是「替代品」，replacement 与 fuel switch 形成同义复现。
C)consumption义指消耗量，与「替代」无关 consumption 表「消耗、消费」，turn to natural gas as a consumption 不通——天然气不是「一种消耗」，而是「煤的替代」。
B) access名词
「__ to power was scarce」做主语，缺主语名词
access to power = 用电的途径 campus coal use has a history dating back to the 1800s when __(29)__ to power was scarce 1800 年代「用电途径稀缺」，故学校自建煤电厂——语义和逻辑都通；access to 是六级听读写都常考的固定搭配。

C)consumptionconsumption of/in，不与 to 搭配 consumption 后通常接 of，「consumption to power」不是英语习惯表达；语义上「电力消费稀缺」也讲不通，因为后文说要自建电厂正是为了「获取电」而非「消费电」。 F)investments复数主语需 were，且 investments to power 不通 investments 是复数，与 was 不一致；且 investments in 才是常见搭配，「投资稀缺」也偏离「为何要自建煤电厂」的因果。
N) surplus形容词
「sell ___ power to utilities」名词 power 前需形容词修饰

surplus power = 剩余电力，正是发电后多余卖给电网的部分 Many universities still operate their own power plants. The Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 encouraged more electricity generation by allowing institutions to sell __(30)__ power to utilities. 大学自办电厂、鼓励多发电——多发出来的电只能是「剩余的」，卖给公共电网（utilities），surplus 完美对应。
O)voidvoid power 语义错位 void 表「无效的、空的」，void power 字面意思偏向「无效电力 / 空的功率」，与「多发的电卖给电网」完全相反。
M) slash动词
「aims to ___ greenhouse gas emissions」不定式 to 后接动词原形
slash emissions = 大幅削减排放，新闻语篇高频搭配 aims to __(31)__ greenhouse gas emissions 与下一句 pledged to be carbon __(32)__ within 20 years 形成「大幅削减 → 实现碳中和」的目标链；slash 表「大幅削减」，正是减排议题中比 reduce 更有力的词。
D)contrivecontrive 多接 to do，不直接带 emissions contrive 表「谋划、设法做成」，常用结构是 contrive to do something，不接 emissions 这类名词宾语；语义上也偏「图谋、设计」，与减排目标不搭。

最具迷惑性的错误词是 D) —— contrive 是动词原形、看似能填 to ___ 位。aims to __(31)__ greenhouse gas emissions 处 contrive 形态正合「to + 动词原形」，且词面冷僻、容易让考生「越冷越对」地误选；但 contrive 不能直接带 emissions 作宾语，语义也偏「图谋」。防坑：减排议题里 to + 动词 + emissions 几乎只配 cut/slash/reduce/curb 这一类「强削减动词」，背主题搭配最稳。
I) neutral形容词
「to be carbon ___ within 20 years」处在不定式 be 的表语位置

carbon neutral = 碳中和，正是减排承诺的目标 About 665 schools are part of the program, which aims to __(31)__ greenhouse gas emissions. Thirty percent of the participants have pledged to be carbon __(32)__ within 20 years. 上一句讲削减温室气体排放，下一句承诺「20 年内 carbon ___」——只有 neutral 能与 carbon 组成减排议题的核心术语，对应「净零排放」。

H)negligent义为「玩忽职守」，与碳排话题不搭 negligent 指人疏忽、失职，从不与 carbon 搭配，语义方向也与「减排承诺」相反。 N)surplus「碳过剩」不是承诺目标 carbon surplus 一来不是固定术语，二来「碳过剩」是要避免的问题，而非「pledged to be」的对象。 O)void「carbon void」非术语、且 void 多与 of 连用 void 作形容词常说 void of/null and void，与 carbon 不构成减排领域的固定搭配，意思也与「碳中和」对不上。
F) investments名词
「withdraw their ___ in coal」中物主代词 their 后 + 介词 in，必为名词

withdraw investments in fossil fuels = 撤资行动 campaigns for universities to withdraw their __(33)__ in coal and other fossil fuels 与 Beyond Coal 运动一致，呼吁大学从化石燃料中「撤资」——withdraw investments in 是经济议题的固定搭配，复数 investments 也与 their 自然搭配。

C)consumption「撤回消费」语义怪 withdraw their consumption in coal 不是英语习惯说法；且后文 22 所高校宣布「move beyond coal」是从资本层面撤离，不只是减少使用。 J)reductions「撤回削减」逻辑反了 reductions 指「削减」，withdraw their reductions 等于「撤回削减」，与全文主旨完全相反——campaigns 的目的不是阻止削减，而是推动撤资以加速脱煤。
J) reductions名词
「The largest coal use ___ at colleges were in Michigan...」主语缺名词中心，谓语 were 提示复数

the largest coal use reductions = 最大的煤炭使用削减量 The largest coal use __(34)__ at colleges were in Michigan, Missouri, Tennessee and Indiana. 与下文 Indiana's universities alone cut coal __(35)__ by 81 percent 同义复现——「削减幅度最大的州」与「印第安纳州削减 81%」对应，reductions 与 cut 是同根名动呼应。
C) consumption名词
「cut coal ___ by 81 percent」动词 cut 后名词 coal 再 + 空 → 名词作 cut 的宾语

coal consumption = 煤炭消耗量，可被 81% 量化 Indiana's universities alone cut coal __(35)__ by 81 percent between 2008 and 2015. 与 American colleges and universities are using 64 percent less coal 形成同义复现——coal consumption 是 using…coal 的名词化表达，与 by 81 percent 完美咬合。
E)duplicationsduplications 与 coal 无搭配关系 duplications 表「复制品、重复」，从不与 coal 搭配，也无法被「by 百分比」量化为能源指标；语义完全偏离主题。

longreading.title: 2022年12月·第3套 英语六级长篇阅读（信息匹配） 第 1 篇 · 36–45 题答案与解析

passages.en: A) In 1913, classical music sparked a riot in Paris. Igor Stravinsky was introducing his revolutionary "Rite of Spring" ballet to the world, with its discordant melodies and unorthodox choreography(编舞), and the purists in the crowd expressed their disapproval loud and clear. It might have been classical music's version of the time Bob Dylan went electric at the Newport Folk Festival. "The noise, fighting, and shouting in the audience got so loud," NPR's music reporter Miles Hoffman said of the Stravinsky debut, "that the choreographer had to shout out the numbers to the dancers so that they knew what they were supposed to do."
passages.zh: 1913年，古典音乐在巴黎引发了一场骚乱。伊戈尔·斯特拉文斯基正通过他具有革命性的芭蕾舞剧《春之祭》向全世界介绍这种艺术形式，其中不协和的旋律和不合常规的编舞引起了观众中守旧派的大声抗议。这或许可以算是古典音乐版的鲍勃·迪伦在纽波特民谣音乐节上改用电声乐器的那一刻。美国国家公共电台的音乐记者迈尔斯·霍夫曼谈到斯特拉文斯基的首演时说：“观众席中的喧闹、争吵和喊叫声越来越大，以至于编舞者不得不向舞者喊出曲目编号，这样他们才能知道自己应该做什么。”

passages.en: B) It's difficult to imagine a similar disturbance occurring today within America's sacred symphony halls. In fact, it's hard to picture any kind of disruptive activity at all (unless someone's cell phone happens to go off, and then you'd better watch your back). A mannerly aura(氛围) hangs over most classical proceedings, and many of the genre's biggest supporters would have it no other way.
passages.zh: 如今，很难想象美国那些神圣的交响音乐厅里会发生类似的骚动。事实上，几乎很难想象那里会出现任何形式的扰乱行为（除非有人碰巧让手机响了起来，那你最好当心了）。大多数古典音乐活动都笼罩着一种彬彬有礼的氛围，而这一流派的许多最坚定支持者不希望情况有任何改变。

passages.en: C) Today, Western audiences for classical music and opera and ballet are almost always well dressed, older, respectful, achingly silent and often very wealthy (one has to be able to afford most tickets). But as many of America's most storied "highbrow"(高雅的) institutions struggle financially—the Philadelphia Orchestra's much-publicized rebound from bankruptcy is just one recent example—classical music fans and theorists are wondering how the medium can weave itself into the 21st century's cultural fabric without sacrificing its integrity.
passages.zh: 如今，西方的古典音乐、歌剧和芭蕾舞观众几乎总是衣着得体、年长、恭敬、安静得令人难受，而且往往非常富有（大多数票价都必须负担得起）。然而，随着美国许多历史悠久的“高雅”机构陷入财务困境——费城交响乐团广受关注的破产重组成功只是最近的一个例子——古典音乐爱好者和理论家们开始思考，在不牺牲其完整性的情况下，这种艺术形式如何融入21世纪的文化结构。

passages.en: D) For example, should we feel OK "clapping" during classical music events, even if nobody else is? Why shouldn't we cheer for something great, like we do at a rock concert? The Huffington Post recently ran a Great Debate on this issue and many commenters came out on the side of silence. "There is no more rewarding experience in life than being part of an audience where everybody is leaning forward in silence, thoroughly carried away by a great performance of a masterpiece," one commenter wrote. "Why is it so difficult for folks to develop an appreciation and understanding for the mannerisms and traditions of classical music?" asked another.
passages.zh: 例如，即使没有其他人鼓掌，我们是否也可以在古典音乐活动中“鼓掌”？我们为什么不能像在摇滚音乐会上那样，为精彩之处喝彩呢？《赫芬顿邮报》最近就这一问题发起了一场大讨论，许多评论者都支持保持安静。一位评论者写道：“人生中没有比成为这样一群观众的一员更令人满足的体验了：每个人都在座位上身体前倾，安静地沉浸在一场伟大的杰作演出中。”另一位则问道：“为什么人们如此难以培养对古典音乐的举止和传统的欣赏与理解呢？”

passages.en: E) The truth is that classical music audiences weren't always so polite. Robert Greenberg, an award-winning composer, said that when Beethoven first performed his 7th Symphony, audiences forced the orchestra to perform encores(重演) of certain movements immediately, applauding wildly. And in the last few decades, he said, many audiences at opera performances have abandoned pretenses, yelling "Bravo" when they feel like it.
passages.zh: 事实上，古典音乐观众并不总是如此礼貌。屡获殊荣的作曲家罗伯特·格林伯格说，贝多芬首次演出他的《第七交响曲》时，观众迫使乐团立即对其中的某些乐章进行返场演出，并疯狂鼓掌。他还说，在过去几十年里，许多歌剧演出的观众已经不再拘泥于表面上的礼节，想喊“好极了”时就喊出来。

passages.en: F) "I don't think there's anything wrong with an audience showing their enthusiasm for a proper moment by applauding, showing their joy," Greenberg said, noting that the stuffiness in concert halls is "one aspect of contemporary concert etiquette" he doesn't understand. "Instead of waiting half an hour to show enthusiasm, why not show it every eight or nine minutes?"
passages.zh: 格林伯格说：“我不认为观众在适当的时刻通过鼓掌来表达热情、表现喜悦有什么不对。”他指出，音乐厅里的拘谨是“当代音乐会礼仪的一个方面”，而这一点他无法理解。“与其等上半个小时才表达热情，为什么不每隔八九分钟就表达一次呢？”

passages.en: G) Until the rules about behavior and clothing change, it's hard to imagine multitudes of young people filling concert halls on their own accord. They're probably more likely to head to Central Park to watch a free performance with a bottle of wine and their friends. "I think anyone should be able to come into a performance dressed any way they like, and be comfortable any way they like, sitting in that seat ready to enjoy themselves," Greenberg said. "Because it's enjoyable."
passages.zh: 在行为和着装规则发生改变之前，很难想象大批年轻人会自发涌入音乐厅。他们更有可能带着一瓶葡萄酒和朋友们一起去中央公园观看免费演出。格林伯格说：“我认为，任何人都应该能够穿着自己喜欢的任何服装来观看演出，以自己感到舒适的方式坐在座位上，准备好享受其中。因为这本来就是令人愉快的。”

passages.en: H) Greenberg stressed that he doesn't want people to start respecting the music less, and he's not suggesting that we "dumb down" the experience. Rather, it's about opening up "access." When operas first instituted subtitles(字幕) during shows, he said, many purists didn't like the idea, believing that the audience should instead study the works before attending. But now it's commonplace to find titles on the seatback in front of you—choose a language, sit back, and understand what's going on.
passages.zh: 格林伯格强调，他并不希望人们减少对音乐的尊重，也不是在建议我们把这种体验“降低难度”。相反，关键在于扩大“接触的机会”。他说，歌剧演出最初采用字幕时，许多守旧派并不喜欢这个想法，认为观众应该在入场前先研究作品。但如今，在你前方座椅的靠背上看到字幕已经很普遍了——选择一种语言，坐下来，然后理解正在发生什么。

passages.en: I) Allison Vulgamore, president of the Philadelphia Orchestra, is certainly looking to the future. She says certain "classics concerts" dedicated to the old masters will always exist, but not every program has to feature Beethoven and Brahms—or even a stage and seats. "We're trying to introduce different kinds of concerts in different ways," she said. "We are an interactive society now, where people like to learn."
passages.zh: 费城交响乐团团长艾莉森·武尔加莫无疑正在着眼于未来。她说，专门献给古代大师作品的某些“经典音乐会”将始终存在，但并不是每个节目都必须安排贝多芬和勃拉姆斯的作品，甚至也不一定要有舞台和座位。“我们正努力以不同的方式推出不同类型的音乐会，”她说。“我们现在生活在一个互动型社会中，人们喜欢学习。”

passages.en: J) As the Philadelphia Orchestra rebounds from its financial straits, it is also aiming to experiment, without alienating the loyalists. Vulgamore pointed to Cirque de la Symphonie, a recent offering in which jugglers(玩杂耍的人) and acrobats(杂技演员) interacted with musicians. An upcoming collaboration with New York City's Ridge Theatre, meanwhile, will feature a "suspended dance installation" and other theatrical elements occurring in conjunction with an orchestral piece.
passages.zh: 费城交响乐团正在摆脱财务困境，同时也力求进行尝试，而不疏远忠实支持者。武尔加莫提到了最近推出的一场名为“交响马戏”的演出，杂耍演员和杂技演员在其中与音乐家进行互动。与此同时，该乐团即将与纽约市的里奇剧院合作，演出内容将包括“悬空舞蹈装置”以及与一部管弦乐作品同时进行的其他戏剧元素。

passages.en: K) The orchestra also continues to offer $25 annual memberships to Philadelphia students, who can buy rush tickets to every concert on the schedule. "Students line up for the concerts they want, and we get roughly 300 or 350 kids a night coming to these. They take any of the open seats available, 5 minutes before the concert starts," Vulgamore said. "It's like the running of the bulls, that energy when the doors open."
passages.zh: 该乐团还继续向费城学生提供每年25美元的会员资格，持有会员资格的学生可以购买演出日程上每一场音乐会的余票。武尔加莫说：“学生们会排队购买他们想看的音乐会的票，每晚大约有300到350个孩子来观看。他们会在音乐会开始前5分钟入场，坐到所有空余的座位上。门一开，那种能量就像奔牛节一样。”

passages.en: L) Greenberg thinks that youthful energy needs to be harvested. Conductors don't have to be arrogant and untouchable—they can be accessible. Perhaps there could even be a "bit of humor" about them, he suggested, and an abandoning of pretension within the high-art institutions themselves. "On one hand, these organizations are all saying the same thing: we want more general audiences, to break down cultural barriers," he said. "But then they come up with some very snooty(目中无人的) thing that makes you crazy."
passages.zh: 格林伯格认为，这种年轻人的活力需要被充分利用。指挥家不必傲慢而让人难以接近——他们可以平易近人。他建议，甚至可以对他们抱有“一点幽默感”，而高雅艺术机构本身也应摒弃矫饰。“一方面，这些机构都在说同样的话：我们想吸引更多普通观众，打破文化壁垒，”他说。“但另一方面，它们又会提出一些非常自命不凡的做法，让人恼火。”

passages.en: M) John Terauds, a critic who has covered Toronto's classical music scene extensively, also wants to do away with the stuffiness. He suggested that the warmer an audience is, the better the musicians themselves will respond. "But the producer or organizer has to let everyone know it's OK," he said. "It's OK to enjoy yourself." At the Toronto Symphony Orchestra, for example, conductor Peter Oundjian often stops between pieces, taking a moment to talk about the composer or the music in a very amiable way. And some nights, Terauds said, "at least a third" of the audience consists of students who have purchased cheaper tickets. On these nights, the energy of the room drastically shifts. It becomes a less intimidating place.
passages.zh: 约翰·特劳兹是一位长期深入报道多伦多古典音乐界的评论家，他也希望消除这种拘谨。他认为，观众越热情，音乐家们本身的回应就会越好。“但制作人或组织者必须让每个人知道，享受演出是可以的，”他说。“尽情享受是可以的。”例如，在多伦多交响乐团，指挥彼得·翁德吉安经常在曲目之间停下来，用非常亲切的方式花片刻时间谈论作曲家或音乐。特劳兹说，有些晚上，观众中“至少三分之一”是购买了低价票的学生。在这些晚上，整个大厅的气氛会发生巨大变化，变成一个不那么令人望而生畏的地方。

passages.en: N) Back in February, Terauds wrote on his blog about how going to classical performances can be intimidating. Certain people "think they have to dress up," he wrote. "They think they have to know something about the music before they go. And, I'm sure, sitting in a seat, trembling in fear that this might be the wrong time to applaud, is also one of the factors."
passages.zh: 早在二月，特劳兹就在他的博客上写道，去观看古典音乐演出可能会让人感到畏惧。他写道，有些人“认为自己必须穿得正式”。“他们认为自己必须在去之前了解一些音乐知识。而且，我敢肯定，坐在座位上战战兢兢，担心现在鼓掌会不会不是合适的时机，也是一项影响因素。”

passages.en: O) Everyone in the classical world agrees on the need for increased "accessibility," but achieving it is often easier said than done. Nowadays, there are unknown, unorthodox opera singers wowing(博得……的喝彩) viewers on TV programs like "America's Got Talent" and "The Voice". What can higher institutions do with any of that? And if they appeal to these outlets, do they risk compromising the integrity or the intelligence of the music?
passages.zh: 古典音乐界的每个人都认同有必要提高“可接近性”，但实现这一点往往说起来容易做起来难。如今，电视节目《美国达人》和《美国之声》中，未曾成名且不拘一格的歌剧歌手正在赢得观众的喝彩。那些高雅艺术机构能从中做些什么呢？而如果它们借助这些平台，是否会冒着损害音乐完整性或思想内涵的风险呢？

passages.en: P) Vulgamore seems to understand this. She thinks an organization can have it both ways, claiming the new while keeping the old. And as she reorganizes the Philadelphia Orchestra, she will attempt to do just that. "The world's most respected musicians brought together as an orchestra will always exist," she said. "But it's essential that we be willing to experiment and fail."
passages.zh: 武尔加莫似乎理解这一点。她认为，一个机构可以两全其美，既拥抱新事物，又保留传统。她在重组费城交响乐团时，将努力做到这一点。“由世界上最受尊敬的音乐家组成的交响乐团将始终存在，”她说。“但关键在于，我们必须愿意进行尝试，也必须愿意接受失败。”

passages.en: How can one person enjoy good health, while another person looks old before her time? Humans have been asking this question for thousands of years, and recently, it's becoming clearer and clearer to scientists that the differences between people's rates of aging lie in the complex interactions among genes, social relationships, environments and lifestyles. Even though you were born with a particular set of genes, the way you live can influence how they express themselves. Some lifestyle factors may even turn genes on or shut them off.
passages.zh: 为什么有些人能够享有良好的健康状况，而另一些人却未老先衰？几千年来，人类一直在追问这个问题。最近，科学家越来越清楚地认识到，人们衰老速度的差异源于基因、社会关系、环境和生活方式之间复杂的相互作用。尽管你出生时拥有一组特定的基因，但你的生活方式会影响这些基因如何表达。某些生活方式因素甚至可能会开启或关闭基因。

passages.en: Deep within the genetic heart of all our cells are telomeres, or repeating segments of noncoding DNA that live at the ends of the chromosomes(染色体). They form caps at the ends of the chromosomes and keep the genetic material together. Shortening with each cell division, they help determine how fast a cell ages. When they become too short, the cell stops dividing altogether. This isn't the only reason a cell can age—there are other stresses on cells we don't yet understand very well—but short telomeres are one of the major reasons human cells grow old. We've devoted most of our careers to studying telomeres, and one extraordinary discovery from our labs is that telomeres can actually lengthen.
passages.zh: 在我们所有细胞的遗传核心深处，存在着端粒，也就是位于染色体末端的、重复排列的非编码DNA片段。它们在染色体末端形成帽状结构，使遗传物质保持完整。端粒会随着每次细胞分裂而缩短，并帮助决定细胞衰老的速度。当端粒变得过短时，细胞就会完全停止分裂。这并不是细胞衰老的唯一原因——细胞还会受到其他我们尚未充分了解的压力——但端粒过短是人类细胞衰老的主要原因之一。我们职业生涯的大部分时间都致力于研究端粒，而我们实验室的一项非凡发现是，端粒实际上能够变长。

passages.en: Scientists have learned that several thought patterns appear to be unhealthy for telomeres, and one of them is cynical hostility. Cynical hostility is defined by high anger and frequent thoughts that other people cannot be trusted. Someone with hostility doesn't just think, "I hate to stand in long lines"; they think, "Others deliberately sped up and beat me to my rightful position in the line!"—and then get violently agitated. People who score high on measures of cynical hostility tend to get more heart disease, metabolic disease and often die at younger ages. They also have shorter telomeres. In a study of British civil servants, men who scored high on measures of cynical hostility had shorter telomeres than men whose hostility scores were low. The most hostile men were 30% more likely to have short telomeres.
passages.zh: 科学家已经了解到，有几种思维模式似乎对端粒不利，其中之一就是愤世嫉俗的敌意。愤世嫉俗的敌意表现为强烈的愤怒，以及经常认为他人不可信的想法。抱有敌意的人并不只是想：“我讨厌排很长的队”；他们会想：“别人是故意加快速度，抢在我前面，占据了本应属于我的排队位置！”然后变得极度激动。愤世嫉俗的敌意测量得分较高的人往往更容易患心脏病和代谢性疾病，而且通常更早死亡。他们的端粒也更短。在一项针对英国公务员的研究中，愤世嫉俗的敌意测量得分较高的男性，其端粒比敌意得分较低的男性更短。敌意最强的男性拥有短端粒的可能性高出30%。

passages.en: What this means: aging is a dynamic process that could possibly be accelerated or slowed—and, in some aspects, even reversed. To an extent, it has surprised us and the rest of the scientific community that telomeres do not simply carry out the commands issued by your genetic code. Your telomeres are listening to you. The foods you eat, your response to challenges, the amount of exercise you get, and many other factors appear to influence your telomeres and can prevent premature aging at the cellular level. One of the keys to enjoying good health is simply doing your part to foster healthy cell renewal.
passages.zh: 这意味着，衰老是一个动态过程，可能会加速或减缓，并且在某些方面甚至可以逆转。端粒并不会简单地执行遗传密码发出的指令，这一点在一定程度上令我们以及科学界其他人士感到惊讶。你的端粒正在倾听你的身体。你所吃的食物、你对挑战的反应、你进行的运动量以及许多其他因素，似乎都会影响你的端粒，并能在细胞层面防止过早衰老。享有良好健康状况的关键之一，就是尽好自己的责任，促进健康的细胞更新。

questions.stem: What have scientists come to know better today?
questions.stem_zh: 科学家们今天对什么有了更深入的了解?

options.text: Why people age at different rates.
options.zh: 人们为什么以不同速度衰老。

options.text: How genes influence the aging process.
options.zh: 基因如何影响衰老过程。

options.text: How various genes express themselves in aging.
options.zh: 各种基因在衰老中如何表达。

options.text: Why people have long been concerned about aging.
options.zh: 人们为什么长期以来一直关注衰老。

questions.判型: What have scientists come to know better today?问的是科学家"已经"了解到的客观事实，要求回原文找事实句，不需要推断。
questions.拆句: 结构平铺直叙：主语scientists + 谓语have come to know（"逐渐了解到"，动词短语作完成时）+ 比较级状语better today。无陷阱，唯一要注意的是come to know是"逐渐认识到"，非"来认识"。
questions.定位: P1 Humans have been asking this question for thousands of years, and recently, it's becoming clearer and clearer to scientists that the differences between people's rates of aging lie in the complex interactions among genes, social relationships, environments and lifestyles. 几千年来人类一直在问这个问题，而最近，科学家越来越清楚地认识到：人与人之间衰老速度的差异，源于基因、社会关系、环境和生活方式之间的复杂互动。

locate.en: Humans have been asking this question for thousands of years, and recently, it's becoming clearer and clearer to scientists that the differences between people's rates of aging lie in the complex interactions among genes, social relationships, environments and lifestyles.

option_analysis.note: 预判"为何人们衰老速度不同"与Why people age at different rates逐词同义对应，且A完整覆盖了定位句的核心信息（差异+原因）。

pairs.opt: Why people age at different rates

option_analysis.note: 定位句只说"差异源于基因等多因素互动"，并未具体阐述"基因如何影响衰老过程"；选项How genes influence the aging process问的是机制原理，是原文没展开的内容。

定位句只点名"基因等因素互动"，原文Even though you were born with a particular set of genes, the way you live can influence how they express themselves.虽提到基因表达，但并未说"各种基因如何在衰老中表达自己"——选项C说的various genes在衰老中"各自如何表达"原文未有此层级讨论。

questions.stem: Why are some lifestyle factors considered extremely important?
questions.stem_zh: 为什么某些生活方式因素被认为极其重要?

options.text: They may shorten the process of cell division.

options.zh: 它们可能决定基因如何发挥作用。

options.text: They may affect the lifespan of telomeres.
options.zh: 它们可能影响端粒的寿命。

options.zh: 它们可能是细胞承受压力的原因。

questions.判型: Why are some lifestyle factors considered extremely important?问的是被认定为重要的客观理由，在原文有对应解释句。
questions.拆句: 被动语态主干lifestyle factors are considered extremely important，相当于"people consider lifestyle factors extremely important"。注意被动里considered是"被认为"，不是"考虑"，读出主动意思即可。

原文谈端粒影响"细胞衰老速度"和"人类细胞何时停止分裂"，但从未上升到the quality of life（生活质量）这一宏观概念——"生活质量"是远超细胞机制的延伸推断。

locate.en: Scientists have learned that several thought patterns appear to be unhealthy for telomeres, and one of them is cynical hostility.

passages.en: Scientists have created by accident an enzyme(酶) that breaks down plastic drinks bottles. The breakthrough could help solve the global plastic pollution crisis by enabling for the first time the full recycling of bottles.
passages.zh: 科学家们意外地制造出了一种能够分解塑料饮料瓶的酶。这一突破有望通过首次实现饮料瓶的完全回收，帮助解决全球塑料污染危机。

passages.en: The new research was spurred by the discovery in 2016 of the first bacterium that had naturally evolved to eat plastic at a waste dump in Japan. Scientists have now revealed the detailed structure of the crucial enzyme produced by the bug.
passages.zh: 这项新研究源于2016年在日本一处垃圾倾倒场发现的第一种能够自然进化出以塑料为食能力的细菌。如今，科学家们已经揭示了这种细菌产生的关键酶的详细结构。

passages.en: An international team then adjusted the enzyme to see how it had evolved, but tests showed they had accidentally made the molecule even better at breaking down the plastic used for drinks bottles. "What actually turned out was we improved the enzyme, which was a bit of a shock," said head researcher Prof. McGeehan, at the University of Portsmouth, UK.
passages.zh: 随后，一个国际团队对这种酶进行了调整，以了解它是如何进化的，但测试显示，他们意外地使这种分子分解饮料瓶所用塑料的能力变得更强了。“实际结果是，我们改进了这种酶，这着实让人震惊，”英国朴次茅斯大学的首席研究员McGeehan教授说。

passages.en: Currently, the enzyme takes a few days to start breaking down the plastic, far faster than the centuries it takes in the oceans, but the researchers are optimistic this can be speeded up even further and become a viable large-scale process.
passages.zh: 目前，这种酶需要几天时间才能开始分解塑料，这已经远快于塑料在海洋中需要数百年才能分解的速度，但研究人员乐观地认为，这一过程还可以进一步加快，并成为一种可行的大规模处理方式。

passages.en: "What we are hoping to do is use this enzyme to turn this plastic back into its original components, so we can literally recycle it back to plastic," said McGeehan. "It means we won't need to dig up any more oil and, fundamentally, it should reduce the amount of plastic in the environment."
passages.zh: “我们希望利用这种酶将塑料还原成其最初的成分，从而真正把它重新制成塑料，实现回收利用，”McGeehan说。“这意味着我们不再需要开采更多石油，而且从根本上说，这应该会减少环境中的塑料数量。”

passages.en: About 1 million plastic bottles are sold each minute around the globe and, with just 14% recycled, many end up in the oceans where they have polluted even the remotest parts, harming marine life and potentially people who eat sea food. "Plastic is incredibly resistant to degradation," said McGeehan. "It is one of these wonder materials that has been made a little bit too well."
passages.zh: 全球每分钟售出约100万个塑料瓶，而其中只有14%得到回收，许多塑料瓶最终流入海洋，污染了甚至最偏远的地区，危害海洋生物，也可能伤害食用海产品的人类。“塑料极其耐降解，”McGeehan说。“它是这类被制造得有些过于完美的神奇材料之一。”

passages.en: Currently those bottles that are recycled can only be turned into opaque fibres for clothing or carpets, while the new enzyme indicates a way to recycle old clear plastic bottles back into new clear plastic bottles.
passages.zh: 目前，回收的塑料瓶只能被制成不透明的服装纤维或地毯纤维，而这种新酶则显示出一条途径，可以将旧的透明塑料瓶重新制成新的透明塑料瓶。

passages.en: "You are always up against the fact oil is cheap, so plastic is cheap," said McGeehan. "It is so easy for manufacturers to generate more of that stuff, rather than even try to recycle, but I believe there is a public interest here: perception is changing so much that companies are starting to look at how they can properly recycle these bottles."
passages.zh: “你始终要面对这样一个事实：石油价格低廉，所以塑料也便宜，”McGeehan说。“制造商很容易生产更多这种材料，甚至无需尝试回收，但我认为这里存在公共利益：人们的观念正在发生巨大变化，因此企业开始考虑如何真正回收这些塑料瓶。”

passages.en: Prof. Adisa Azapagic, at the University of Manchester in the UK, agreed the enzyme could be useful but added: "A full life-cycle assessment would be needed to ensure that the technology does not solve one environmental problem—waste—at the expense of others, including additional greenhouse gas emissions."
passages.zh: 英国曼彻斯特大学的Adisa Azapagic教授同意这种酶可能会有用，但她补充说：“还需要进行完整的生命周期评估，以确保这项技术不会以增加其他环境问题为代价来解决某一个环境问题——废弃物问题，其中包括额外的温室气体排放。”

translation.title: 2022年12月·第3套英语六级汉译英（段落翻译） · 客观介绍云贵高原的地理与人文 参考译文与解析
translation.directions: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to translate a passage from Chinese into English. You should write your answer on Answer Sheet 2.
translation.source_zh: 云贵高原(the Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau)大部分位于云南、贵州省境内，总面积约50万平方公里，平均海拔2000-4000米，是中国第四大高原。云贵高原西高东低，河流众多，形成了许多又深又陡的峡谷(canyon)。 峡谷中许多地方土壤肥沃，非常有利于多种农作物生长。 云贵高原独特的自然环境造就了生物和文化的多样性。它是中国森林和矿产资源类型十分丰富的地区，也是古人类起源的重要地区。云贵高原是中国少数民族数量最多的地区，各民族都保留了自己丰富多彩的文化传统。
translation.reference_en:
Located mostly in Yunnan Province and Guizhou Province, the Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau, with a total area of about 500,000 square kilometers and an average altitude of 2,000 to 4,000 meters, is the fourth largest plateau in China. High in the west and low in the east, the plateau is crisscrossed by numerous rivers, which have carved out many deep and steep canyons. In many parts of these canyons, the soil is fertile, which is highly favorable for the growth of various crops. Such a unique natural environment has given rise to rich biological and cultural diversity. It is a region rich in various types of forest and mineral resources in China, and it is also an important area for the origin of ancient humans. The Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau is home to the largest number of ethnic minorities in China, where each ethnic group has preserved its own rich and colorful cultural traditions.
【衔接】
第4句承上启下，用衔接词点出转折第3句讲峡谷土壤利于农作物，第4句 云贵高原独特的自然环境造就了生物和文化的多样性 是把前面地形、土壤的描述收束、升华到'多样性'这一主题。可在第4句句首补 Such a unique natural environment… 或用 Moreover / In addition 显出递进，让'从具体地貌过渡到宏观多样性'的层次清晰。

末句回扣专名收束全篇前面已多次用 It / the plateau 指代，末句 云贵高原是中国少数民族数量最多的地区 重新点出 The Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau 全名作收束、首尾呼应，比再用一次 It 更有'结尾感'，让整篇有明确的落点。

main_idea.core: 客观介绍云贵高原的地理与人文
main_idea.detail: 全篇是一段客观的地理科普介绍，围绕云贵高原的位置、面积、海拔、地形、资源与民族文化展开，属于典型的「中国地理/文化介绍」语体。开篇 云贵高原(the Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau)大部分位于云南、贵州省境内，总面积约50万平方公里，平均海拔2000-4000米，是中国第四大高原 就是在陈述一个长期稳定的客观事实，不是在叙述某段历史事件，这直接决定了下面的时态基调与平实的用词风格。

tense.detail: 通篇都在陈述云贵高原现在仍然成立的客观特征（位置、面积、地形、资源、民族），是「描述事物现状与属性」而非「叙述过去发生的事」，所以全篇默认用一般现在时。例如 是中国第四大高原、各民族都保留了自己丰富多彩的文化传统 说的都是至今仍然如此的状态。

term_notes.detail: 原文已直接给出官方英文译名，统一用 the Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau，全篇出现处一律照此，不要时而写 Yunnan-Guizhou、时而写 Yun-Gui。依据：云贵高原(the Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau)，括号内即约定俗成译名，照抄即可。
采用「拼音 + 通名」的约定俗成译法：Yunnan Province 与 Guizhou Province。省份名音译，Province 首字母大写。依据 大部分位于云南、贵州省境内。
原文已给出对应词 canyon，统一用 canyon(s)。第 2 句首次出现的「许多峡谷」用复数 canyons，第 3 句回指时用 the canyons / these canyons，保持同一个词。依据 形成了许多又深又陡的峡谷(canyon)。
统一译为 ethnic minorities（不要用带贬义争议的旧译）；「各民族」指这些少数民族，回指时用 these ethnic groups 或 each ethnic group。依据 云贵高原是中国少数民族数量最多的地区。

steps.text: 以高原为主语的并列陈述（主语策略：原句主语）中文主语明确就是 云贵高原，全句围绕它陈述四项信息。可把核心立为 The Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau is located in… / is China's fourth largest plateau，主语 The Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau，谓语用 is located / is，宾语/表语是位置和「第四大高原」。其余「面积」「海拔」两项作补充信息处理。

数据信息降级为插入/分句本句一口气堆了四个信息点，不能用 and 平铺成一长串。把 大部分位于云南、贵州省境内 作主干 (is mostly located in…)；总面积约50万平方公里，平均海拔2000-4000米 这两项数据降级，用 with 引导的伴随介词短语 with a total area of about 500,000 square kilometers and an average altitude of 2,000 to 4,000 meters 挂在主干后；是中国第四大高原 作收尾的并列表语，用分号或 and it is… 收束。

时态回指全篇基调，陈述客观地理事实，用一般现在时 is located / is，不要用过去时。 数字表达50万平方公里写作 500,000 square kilometers（不是 50 万直译 fifty ten-thousand）；海拔区间 2000-4000 米写作 2,000 to 4,000 meters，用 to 表区间。 单复数与冠词fourth largest plateau 是序数词最高级，前面必须加 the：China's fourth largest plateau 或 the fourth largest plateau in China。square kilometers、meters 复数。

Located mostly in Yunnan Province and Guizhou Province, the Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau, with a total area of about 500,000 square kilometers and an average altitude of 2,000 to 4,000 meters, is the fourth largest plateau in China.

高原作主语贯穿三个分句（主语策略：原句主语）三个分句 西高东低，河流众多，形成了许多又深又陡的峡谷 共享同一主语'云贵高原'。最核心的动作是'形成了…峡谷'，故主干立为 The plateau has formed many canyons / many canyons have formed，主语 The plateau，谓语 form，宾语 canyons；'西高东低''河流众多'是造成峡谷的背景条件。

地势与成因降级为状语西高东低 是地势特征，可处理成主句前的状语分句 Higher in the west and lower in the east 或 With its terrain高 in the west…；河流众多 是密集成因，与'形成峡谷'是因果，可降级为 with numerous rivers 的伴随短语，或译成 where numerous rivers… 引出。'又深又陡'作 canyons 的前置定语 deep and steep。整句重构为：地势状语 + 主干（众多河流形成了又深又陡的峡谷）。

时态'形成了'虽带'了'，但描述的是至今仍存在的地貌结果，用一般现在时 forms / has formed 均可，与全篇现在时基调一致；推荐 has formed 兼顾'已形成且仍在'，但保持一般现在时 form 也对，关键是不要用一般过去时 formed（会读成过去一次性事件）。 单复数'许多峡谷'是复数 many canyons；'河流众多'是 numerous rivers，均用复数，呼应'许多/众多'。 形容词并列'又深又陡'两个形容词并列修饰 canyons，用 deep and steep，置于名词前作定语。
High in the west and low in the east, the plateau is crisscrossed by numerous rivers, which have carved out many deep and steep canyons.
以土壤肥沃为主、利于生长为果（主语策略：原句主语）中文有明确主语 峡谷中许多地方，核心陈述是'土壤肥沃'。可立主干 The soil is fertile（主语 the soil，系动词 is，表语 fertile），或以 many places 作主语 Many places… have fertile soil。'非常有利于…生长'是这肥沃带来的结果，作后续。

有利于生长降级为结果状语非常有利于多种农作物生长 不另起一句，而降级为表结果的成分：可用 which is very favorable for the growth of various crops 定语从句，或 making it ideal for growing various crops 的现在分词结果状语挂在主干后。'多种农作物'译 various / a variety of crops。

时态陈述土壤的客观属性，回指全篇一般现在时 is fertile / is favorable。 单复数与不可数名词soil（土壤）作'土壤'整体义时为不可数名词，用 the soil、不加复数；crops（农作物）是可数，'多种'用复数 various crops。 介词搭配'有利于'后接对象用 favorable for / beneficial to；'有利于…生长'用 favorable for the growth of… 或 for growing…，介词不要错配成 favorable to growth。
In many parts of these canyons, the soil is fertile, which is highly favorable for the growth of various crops.
环境作主语造就多样性（主语策略：原句主语）中文是标准的'施事 + 动作 + 宾语'结构：主语 云贵高原独特的自然环境，谓语'造就了'，宾语'生物和文化的多样性'。直接对译主干 The unique natural environment has created/given rise to biological and cultural diversity，主谓宾一一对应。
本句结构简单无需大改本句是单一主谓宾的简单句，无多余分句要降级。唯一处理是把'独特的'作前置定语 unique 修饰 natural environment，'生物和文化的'作并列定语 biological and cultural 修饰 diversity。结构上照搬即可，重点在选准'造就了'的英文动词。

时态'造就了'描述至今仍存在的多样性，用现在完成时 has created / has given rise to 或一般现在时 creates 皆可，与全篇基调统一，不用一般过去时。 单复数与不可数名词diversity（多样性）为不可数名词，不加 s；environment 特指这片高原的环境，用 the unique natural environment 加 the。 并列定语'生物和文化的多样性'即'生物多样性和文化多样性'，用 biological and cultural diversity，两个形容词并列共享 diversity。
The unique natural environment of the Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau has given rise to rich biological and cultural diversity.
代词它作主语的双重定性（主语策略：原句主语）主语是承接上句的代词 它（指云贵高原），用 It 即可。本句是'它是 A，也是 B'的双重定性：主干 It is a region…（系动词 is + 表语 region），两个'地区'用并列结构 It is… and also…连接。

两重身份用并列表语处理中国森林和矿产资源类型十分丰富的地区 中'森林和矿产资源类型十分丰富'是 region 的修饰，用 with rich types of forest and mineral resources 介词短语，或 rich in forest and mineral resources 后置；古人类起源的重要地区 用 an important area for the origin of ancient humans。两个'地区'用 It is… and also… 并列，避免重复主语。

时态客观定性，回指全篇一般现在时 It is…。 单复数'资源类型'用 types of… resources，types 复数；forest and mineral resources 中 resources 复数；'地区'两处可用 a region / an area，单数加冠词。 冠词两个'地区'是泛指其中一类，用不定冠词 a region / an important area；an 用在元音音素 important 前。
It is a region rich in various types of forest and mineral resources in China, and it is also an important area for the origin of ancient humans.

两个分句各有主语（主语策略：原句主语）本句含两个主语不同的分句：前句 云贵高原是中国少数民族数量最多的地区，主语云贵高原（可用 It 承接），主干 It is the region with the largest number of ethnic minorities；后句 各民族都保留了自己丰富多彩的文化传统，主语换成'各民族'，主干 each ethnic group preserves its cultural traditions。两分句不共主语，需各立主谓。

后句用where从句衔接前句前句 数量最多的地区 用最高级 the largest number of…；后句 各民族都保留了自己丰富多彩的文化传统 与前句是'在这个地区里，各民族…'的关系，最自然是用 where 引导定语从句把后句挂到 region 上：…the largest number of ethnic minorities, where each group preserves its colorful cultural traditions。'丰富多彩的'作定语 colorful / rich and colorful。

时态'保留了'的'了'同样指至今仍保留的状态，用一般现在时 preserves / retain 或现在完成时 have preserved，与全篇基调统一，不用一般过去时。 最高级与冠词'数量最多'用最高级 the largest number of，前面必须加 the。 主谓一致与单复数ethnic minorities / ethnic groups 复数；若用 each ethnic group 作主语，each 后接单数名词、谓语用单数 preserves its…；若用 various ethnic groups 则谓语用复数 preserve their…，主谓与代词须一致。
The Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau is home to the largest number of ethnic minorities in China, where each ethnic group has preserved its own rich and colorful cultural traditions.
